motions.item_title: Approve the appointment of Susan Allen to the Senior Advisory Board through December 31, 2025
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to approve the appointment of Susan Allen to the Senior Advisory Board through December 31, 2025. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Susan Allen joins the Senior Advisory Board
motions.summary: The council appointed Susan Allen to the Senior Advisory Board for a term running through December 31, 2025.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this fills a seat on a volunteer advisory board through the end of the year.

motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to adopt the Consent Agenda removing items 13.A. and 13.C. to be placed on the Scheduled Items for further discussion. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent agenda approved, two items pulled
motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda but pulled the Transportation Master Plan and a fee reduction request out for separate discussion.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this is the housekeeping step that clears routine items in one vote and sets two aside for fuller debate.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Transportation Master Plan
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Transportation Master Plan. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Transportation Master Plan adopted
motions.summary: The council adopted the Transportation Master Plan, the city's long-range blueprint for which roads Eagle Mountain builds and widens as it grows.
motions.impact: Nothing changes on your street tomorrow, but this plan is what the city points to when deciding which roads get built or widened and what developers must put in.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Fee Reduction Request of Steve McCleery for a Rezone Application from $1,350 to $760
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to deny a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Fee Reduction Request of Steve McCleery for a Rezone Application from $1,350 to $760. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Discount on a rezone fee turned down
motions.summary: The council declined Steve McCleery's request to cut the fee for his rezone application from $1,350 to $760.
motions.impact: Only the applicant is affected — he pays the full $1,350. The city's rezone application fee is unchanged for everyone else.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 16.20 Preliminary Plats and 16.25 Final Plats
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 16.20 Preliminary Plats and 16.25 Final Plats. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Subdivision plat rules amended
motions.summary: The council amended the city's rules for preliminary and final plats — the approval steps land must clear before it can be split into lots.
motions.impact: This changes the process for developers and anyone subdividing land; the motion does not spell out what the new rules require. Existing homeowners see no change.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.100 Site Plans and omitting the proposed redline in 17.100.130 section “D” number nine (changing the exterior finishing materials from one acceptable material to another acceptable material as listen in the standards in the zone)
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.100 Site Plans and omitting the proposed redline in 17.100.130 section “D” number nine (changing the exterior finishing materials from one acceptable material to another acceptable material as listen in the standards in the zone). Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Site plan rules updated for new development
motions.summary: The council updated the city's site plan rules but left out a proposed change covering the swap of one approved exterior building material for another.
motions.impact: This touches builders and businesses going through site plan review, who must still get sign-off to change approved exterior materials. If you are not developing property, nothing changes for you.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Repealing and Reenacting Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 2.45 Youth Council
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Repealing and Reenacting Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 2.45 Youth Council with changes as follows: • Include “Youth” Mayor when referring to the Youth Mayor and “Mayor” when referring to the appointed City Mayor, • In Section 2.45.040 Subsection E, committee approval by the City Manager will be replaced by Youth Council Committee of Advisors. • In Section 2.45.040 Subsection A.8., include “Elected City Mayor” when coordinating all activities with the Youth Council Committee of Advisors. • In 2.45.010 Section C: Change from “members are appointed to Youth Council by the City Manager” to “members are appointed by the Youth Council Committee of Advisors”. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Youth Council rules adopted with mayor voting
motions.summary: With the mayor included in the vote, the council adopted the rewritten Youth Council rules, shifting appointment of youth members to a committee of advisors.
motions.impact: This affects the teens on the Youth Council and how they are chosen. Nothing changes for other residents.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Disposal of 0.156 Acres of Designated "Significant Real Property" (Utah County Parcel #49:601:0080) Pursuant to EMMC 3.30.060 and 3.30.070, and Establishing Terms of the Disposal
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Disposal of 0.156 Acres of Designated "Significant Real Property" (Utah County Parcel #49:601:0080) Pursuant to EMMC 3.30.060 and 3.30.070, and Establishing Terms of the Disposal with terms below: • Approving option two with each landowner of the parcels listed signing the land disposal application. The applicants may combine the application into one land disposal application and fee. • If any landowner, in any of the lots are unwilling or unable to purchase the corresponding parcels, the approval will revert to option one. • It is required that all fences are on the correct lot line or the lots are to have no fence within 6 months of recordation. • The water requirements for each parcel are fulfilled with the purchase of the parcels as deemed appropriate by staff. • The full land disposal application and process must be finalized in six months (February 19, 2026). Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: City to sell a small parcel to adjoining owners
motions.summary: The city approved selling 0.156 acres of city-owned land to the owners of the neighboring lots, with the sale to be finished by February 19, 2026.
motions.impact: Only the owners of the adjoining lots are affected. They can buy the parcels together on one application, and within six months their fences must sit on the correct lot line or be removed.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Providing for a Referendum to be held on November 4, 2025, for the purpose of submitting to the qualified voters of Eagle Mountain City, Utah County, Utah the question of authorization of the imposition a 0.1% sales and use tax (one-tenth of one percent) for the purpose of funding recreational, cultural, botanical, and zoological facilities, and botanical, cultural, and zoological organizations within the City (RAP Tax)
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Providing for a Referendum to be held on November 4, 2025, for the purpose of submitting to the qualified voters of Eagle Mountain City, Utah County, Utah the question of authorization of the imposition a 0.1% sales and use tax (one-tenth of one percent) for the purpose of funding recreational, cultural, botanical, and zoological facilities, and botanical, cultural, and zoological organizations within the City (RAP Tax). Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: RAP tax question goes to voters in November
motions.summary: The council put a 0.1% sales tax for recreation, arts, and cultural facilities on the November 4, 2025 ballot.
motions.impact: You decide this one at the polls. If it passes, you would pay an extra 10 cents on every $100 spent in the city, with the money going to recreation and cultural facilities.

motions.item_title: Place archery shooting at the Rodeo Grounds to the Legislative Priorities List
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to place archery shooting at the Rodeo Grounds to the Legislative Priorities List. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Push to allow archery at the Rodeo Grounds
motions.summary: The council added allowing archery shooting at the city's Rodeo Grounds to its legislative priorities list.
motions.impact: Nothing changes at the Rodeo Grounds for now. This puts archery on the city's list of things to pursue; it does not by itself open a place to shoot.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Repealing and Reenacting Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 2.45 Youth Council City Attorney Marcus Draper stated Item 15.A. needed to be recalled because Mayor Westmoreland was not included in the vote for Repealing and Reenacting Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 2.45 Youth Council as required by City Code. Councilmember Gray moved to reconsider Item 15.A. Councilmembers then moved to adopt Item 15.A. and included the Mayor.
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to reconsider Item 15.A., an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Repealing and Reenacting Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 2.45 Youth Council. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Youth Council vote redone to include the mayor
motions.summary: The council reopened its vote on the Youth Council rules after the city attorney said city code requires the mayor to be included in it.
motions.impact: This is a procedural do-over to make the vote valid. The ordinance itself did not change, and nothing changes for residents.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Repealing and Reenacting Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 2.45 Youth Council with changes as follows: • Include “Youth” Mayor when referring to the Youth Mayor and “Mayor” when referring to the appointed City Mayor, • In Section 2.45.040 Subsection E, committee approval by the City Manager will be replaced by Youth Council Committee of Advisors. • In Section 2.45.040 Subsection A.8., include “Elected City Mayor” when coordinating all activities with the Youth Council Committee of Advisors. • In 2.45.010 Section C: Change from “members are appointed to Youth Council by the City Manager” to “members are appointed by the Youth Council Committee of Advisors”
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to adopt Item 15.A., an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Repealing and Reenacting Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 2.45 Youth Council with changes as follows: • Include “Youth” Mayor when referring to the Youth Mayor and “Mayor” when referring to the appointed City Mayor, • In Section 2.45.040 Subsection E, committee approval by the City Manager will be replaced by Youth Council Committee of Advisors. • In Section 2.45.040 Subsection A.8., include “Elected City Mayor” when coordinating all activities with the Youth Council Committee of Advisors. • In 2.45.010 Section C: Change from “members are appointed to Youth Council by the City Manager” to “members are appointed by the Youth Council Committee of Advisors”. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Youth Council rules rewritten
motions.summary: The council rewrote the rules for the city's Youth Council, moving the power to appoint youth members from the city manager to a committee of advisors.
motions.impact: This affects the teens who serve on the Youth Council and the adults who run it. Nothing changes for other residents.

motions.item_title: Add Veterans and Active-Duty Military Public Servants and Military to the Mortgage Assistance P…
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to add Veterans and Active-Duty Military Public Servants and Military to the Mortgage Assistance Program for the Legislative Priority List. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Ask lawmakers to open mortgage aid to veterans
motions.summary: The council put expanding the mortgage assistance program to veterans, active-duty military, and public servants on its list of state legislative priorities.
motions.impact: Nothing changes yet — this only tells state lawmakers what Eagle Mountain wants. Any actual home-buying help for veterans and military families would have to come from the Legislature.
